edits.after: 2.2 The attained list maximum argument in step 1.1 makes the maximizing-action set nonempty at every state. By [A1], choose one such action at every state and call the resulting deterministic stationary policy $\pi^*$. Define its stationary probability-family embedding by $\widehat\pi^*(b\mid s)=\mathbf1_{\{b=\pi^*(s)\}}$ for $b\in A(s)$. These numbers are nonnegative and sum to one because exactly one legal action equals $\pi^*(s)$, so $\widehat\pi^*$ is a stationary Markov policy in [F5]–[F8]. Its policy Bellman sum has only the chosen maximizing action as a nonzero term. The definitions [F4]–[F5] and $T^*V^*=V^*$ give $T^{\widehat\pi^*}V^*=V^*$. By [F6] this is the unique fixed point of $T^{\widehat\pi^*}$, while [F8] gives $T^{\widehat\pi^*}V^{\widehat\pi^*}=V^{\widehat\pi^*}$; hence $V^{\widehat\pi^*}=V^*$. [A1, F4, F5, F6, F8, step 1.1]

edits.before: 5.1 Construct a continuation with initial pair $(s,a)$ and thereafter action $\pi^*(S_{n+1})$ following each transition. Take $E_0=D$ and $E_{n+1}=\mathcal R\times D$ with their discrete sigma-algebras, initial law concentrated at $(s,a)$, and history kernels $K_n(h,B)=\sum_{s',\rho}p(s',\rho\mid s_n,a_n)\mathbf1_B(\rho,(s',\pi^*(s')))$ for every measurable $B\subseteq E_{n+1}$, where $(s_n,a_n)$ is the last pair in $h$. For disjoint sets $B_j\subseteq E_{n+1}$, their preimages $\{(s',\rho):(\rho,(s',\pi^*(s')))\in B_j\}$ are disjoint subsets of the finite set $S\times\mathcal R$, so only finitely many are nonempty and the finite mass formula is countably additive; its total mass is one by [F1]. It is measurable in $h$ because it is a finite sum of functions of the current-pair coordinate projection, which is measurable by [F18]. Thus each $K_n$ is a probability kernel by [F19], and [F9] gives a path law with these prefix products. Set $\mathcal F_n=\sigma(X_0,Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)$, where $X_0=(S_0,A_0)$ and $Y_j=(R_j,(S_j,A_j))$. The coordinate projections make current pairs measurable at time $n$ and next observations measurable at time $n+1$ by [F18]. The finite history-coordinate set is finite by [F20], so each atom of $\mathcal F_n$ fixes a finite history. On a positive-mass atom ending at $(s_n,a_n)$, the prefix product in [F9] shows that extending it by reward $\rho$, state $s'$, and next action $\pi^*(s')$ has conditional probability $p(s',\rho\mid s_n,a_n)$; all other next-action extensions have conditional probability zero. Thus the conditional probability of $\{R_{n+1}=\rho,S_{n+1}=s'\}$ given $\mathcal F_n$ is $p(s',\rho\mid S_n,A_n)$ on every positive-mass atom, which proves the required almost-sure conditional identity. Hence this process is admissible. By the product form of the finite-prefix probabilities, after the first transition its conditional continuation from $S_1=s'$ has the stationary-policy prefix laws in [F10], so [F7] identifies its conditional expected discounted tail as $V^{\pi^*}(s')$. The expectation convergence proved for every admissible continuation in step 4.1 passes this prefix identity to the infinite return. Therefore $E[G]=\sum_{s',\rho}p(s',\rho\mid s,a)[\rho+\gamma V^{\pi^*}(s')]=Q^\dagger(s,a)$ by step 2.2. This admissible continuation attains the upper bound, so $Q_{\mathrm{opt}}(s,a)=Q^\dagger(s,a)$ and the supremum is a finite maximum. [F1, F7, F9, F10, F18, F19, F20, step 4.1, step 2.2, construct]
